```{r setup}
# The 30-45 minute talk: the data-sources deck and the analysis (Ghana) deck combined,
# with the illustrated concept slides drawn in place by scripts/concept_slides/ from
# MN-proxy-full-talk-2026-09.concept.yaml. Every figure is drawn from the result tables
# at render time, every number in the text, the notes AND the concept slides is an
# expression over the same `Q` list below, so a pipeline re-run followed by
#   bash scripts/render_deck.sh docs/slides/MN-proxy-full-talk-2026-09.qmd --text 18,10 \
#        --concept docs/slides/MN-proxy-full-talk-2026-09.concept.yaml
# refreshes the whole deck. Concept slides are a title plus speaker notes here; their
# content lives in the YAML. The setup is the Ghana deck's chunk followed by the
# data-sources deck's additions (tiers, alignment, spine, exclusions, recurrence).
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(knitr); library(ggplot2)})
root <- tryCatch(here::here(), error = function(e) normalizePath(file.path(getwd(), "..", "..")))
P2 <- file.path(root, "results", "tables", "protocol_v2")
CL <- file.path(root, "results", "tables", "cluster_level")
rd <- function(...) { f <- file.path(...); if (file.exists(f)) read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE) else NULL }
kb <- function(d, digits = 3, ...) knitr::kable(d, format = "pipe", digits = digits, row.names = FALSE, ...)
df <- function(...) data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
f2 <- function(x, d = 2) ifelse(is.finite(x), formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d), "NA")
pc <- function(x, d = 0) ifelse(is.finite(x), paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%"), "NA")
sgn <- function(x, d = 2) ifelse(is.finite(x), paste0(ifelse(x >= 0, "+", ""), formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)), "NA")
get1 <- function(x) if (length(x) && is.finite(x[1])) x[1] else NA_real_

# mean over cells with a 95% interval across cells (normal approximation over the cell values)
cell_ci <- function(d, val, by) {
  d |> group_by(across(all_of(by))) |>
    summarise(n = sum(is.finite(.data[[val]])), est = mean(.data[[val]], na.rm = TRUE),
              se = sd(.data[[val]], na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(pmax(n, 1)), lo = est - 1.96 * se, hi = est + 1.96 * se,
              pos = sum(.data[[val]] > 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
}
forest <- function(d, y, facet = NULL, null = 0, xlab = "Spearman (mean over cells, 95% interval)", base = 15, colour = NULL) {
  g <- ggplot(d, aes(x = est, y = .data[[y]])) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = null, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.25, colour = "grey35", orientation = "y")
  g <- if (is.null(colour)) g + geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#1f4e79") else g + geom_point(aes(colour = .data[[colour]]), size = 3)
  g <- g + labs(x = xlab, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = base) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
  if (!is.null(facet)) g <- g + facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", facet)), scales = "free_x")
  g
}
tlab <- c(level = "Biomarker level", prev = "Prevalence")
olab <- c(child_vitA = "Child vitamin A", women_vitA = "Women's vitamin A", child_iron = "Child iron", women_iron = "Women's iron",
          women_folate = "Women's folate", women_b12 = "Women's B12", child_zinc = "Child zinc", women_zinc = "Women's zinc")
arm_label <- c(domain_index = "Zero-tuning domain index", spatial_plus_domain = "Spatial smoother + covariates", spatial = "Spatial smoother",
               domain_enet = "Elastic net, domain components", raw_enet = "Elastic net, all columns",
               region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean", null_train_mean = "Training mean")

MD  <- rd(root, "data", "covariates", "harmonized", "predictors_admin2_shared_metadata.csv")
BM  <- rd(P2, "benchmarks_v2_summary.csv"); BC <- rd(P2, "benchmarks_v2_cells.csv")
A1  <- rd(P2, "admin1_transport.csv"); CS1 <- rd(P2, "climate_soil_admin1.csv"); ND <- rd(P2, "nested_domain_selection.csv"); NC <- rd(P2, "transport_null_calibration.csv")
WS  <- rd(P2, "weight_sources_cells.csv"); NT <- rd(P2, "nce_targeting_metrics.csv"); NTS <- rd(P2, "nce_targeting_summary.csv")
DA  <- rd(P2, "domain_ablation_loco.csv"); SA <- rd(P2, "source_ablation_loco.csv"); SAS <- rd(P2, "source_ablation_loco_summary.csv")
TC  <- rd(P2, "training_country_curve.csv"); TCS <- rd(P2, "training_curve_climate_soil.csv")
UR  <- rd(P2, "urbanicity_conditioning.csv"); VC <- rd(P2, "variance_components_ceiling.csv"); AR <- rd(P2, "anchor_and_rank.csv")
CV  <- rd(CL, "cluster_vs_district.csv"); MBG <- rd(CL, "mbg_comparison_cells.csv"); TCLU <- rd(CL, "targets_cluster.csv")
RC  <- rd(P2, "risk_category_accuracy.csv"); IL <- rd(P2, "individual_level_models.csv"); IO <- rd(P2, "iodine_in_country.csv")
IT  <- rd(P2, "index_importance_top.csv"); IP <- rd(P2, "index_importance_patterns.csv"); ID <- rd(P2, "index_importance_domains.csv")
TG  <- rd(P2, "targets_v2.csv"); SY <- rd(root, "metadata", "survey_years.csv"); NE <- rd(root, "results", "tables", "national_estimates_all.csv")
SLR <- rd(P2, "sl_rank_loss_scores.csv"); SLH <- rd(P2, "sl_domain_index_scores_hapc.csv"); LI <- rd(P2, "addon_lsms_flunet_infill.csv")
SIG <- rd(root, "results", "tables", "signal_probes", "p4_admin1_continuous_predictors.csv")

# ---- quantities used in the text -------------------------------------------------------
Q <- list()
bm <- function(est, tg, arm, col = "mean_spearman") if (is.null(BM)) NA_real_ else get1(BM[[col]][BM$estimand == est & BM$target == tg & BM$arm == arm])
Q$n_pred <- if (is.null(MD)) NA else nrow(MD); Q$n_dom <- if (is.null(MD)) NA else length(unique(MD$domain))
Q$n_cells <- if (is.null(TG)) NA else nrow(distinct(TG, country, outcome))
Q$n_districts <- if (is.null(TG)) NA else nrow(distinct(TG, country, Admin1, Admin2))
Q$n_clusters <- if (is.null(TCLU)) NA else nrow(distinct(TCLU, country, cluster))
Q$infill_index <- bm("infill", "level", "domain_index"); Q$infill_index_p <- bm("infill", "prev", "domain_index")
Q$infill_jk <- bm("infill", "level", "region_mean_jk"); Q$infill_jk_p <- bm("infill", "prev", "region_mean_jk")
Q$infill_sp <- bm("infill", "level", "spatial"); Q$infill_spd <- bm("infill", "level", "spatial_plus_domain")
Q$infill_enet <- bm("infill", "level", "domain_enet"); Q$infill_raw <- bm("infill", "level", "raw_enet")
Q$region_index <- bm("region", "level", "domain_index"); Q$region_index_p <- bm("region", "prev", "domain_index")
Q$region_sp <- bm("region", "level", "spatial"); Q$region_enet_p <- bm("region", "prev", "domain_enet"); Q$region_raw_p <- bm("region", "prev", "raw_enet")
Q$tr_index <- bm("country", "level", "domain_index"); Q$tr_index_p <- bm("country", "prev", "domain_index")
Q$tr_index_pos <- bm("country", "level", "domain_index", "cells_positive"); Q$tr_index_pos_p <- bm("country", "prev", "domain_index", "cells_positive")
Q$tr_enet <- bm("country", "level", "domain_enet"); Q$tr_enet_pos <- bm("country", "level", "domain_enet", "cells_positive")
Q$tr_cells <- bm("country", "level", "domain_index", "cells")
Q$tr_a1 <- if (is.null(A1)) NA else get1(mean(A1$spearman[A1$arm == "domain_index" & A1$target == "level"], na.rm = TRUE))
Q$tr_a1_p <- if (is.null(A1)) NA else get1(mean(A1$spearman[A1$arm == "domain_index" & A1$target == "prev"], na.rm = TRUE))
Q$tr_a1_pos <- if (is.null(A1)) NA else sum(A1$spearman[A1$arm == "domain_index" & A1$target == "level"] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
Q$cs_d <- if (is.null(ND)) NA else get1(mean(ND$spearman[ND$arm == "fixed_cs" & ND$target == "level"], na.rm = TRUE))
Q$cs_d_pos <- if (is.null(ND)) NA else sum(ND$spearman[ND$arm == "fixed_cs" & ND$target == "level"] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
Q$cs_d_p <- if (is.null(ND)) NA else get1(mean(ND$spearman[ND$arm == "fixed_cs" & ND$target == "prev"], na.rm = TRUE))
Q$cs_a1 <- if (is.null(CS1)) NA else get1(mean(CS1$spearman[CS1$set == "climate_soil" & CS1$target == "level"], na.rm = TRUE))
Q$cs_a1_pos <- if (is.null(CS1)) NA else sum(CS1$spearman[CS1$set == "climate_soil" & CS1$target == "level"] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
Q$nested_vs_full <- if (is.null(ND)) NA else { w <- ND |> filter(target == "level", arm %in% c("full", "nested")) |> select(outcome, heldout, arm, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = spearman); get1(median(w$nested - w$full, na.rm = TRUE)) }
Q$nested_better <- if (is.null(ND)) NA else { w <- ND |> filter(target == "level", arm %in% c("full", "nested")) |> select(outcome, heldout, arm, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = spearman); sum(w$nested > w$full, na.rm = TRUE) }
Q$null_d <- if (is.null(NC)) NA else get1(NC$null_mean_q95[NC$tier == "admin2"]); Q$null_a1 <- if (is.null(NC)) NA else get1(NC$null_mean_q95[NC$tier == "admin1"])
Q$null_pos95 <- if (is.null(NC)) NA else get1(NC$null_positive_q95[NC$tier == "admin2"])
# in-fill: index vs jackknifed regional mean, cells better (level)
if (!is.null(BC)) { w <- BC |> filter(estimand == "infill", target == "level", arm %in% c("domain_index", "region_mean_jk", "spatial")) |> select(country, outcome, arm, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = spearman)
  Q$infill_beats_jk <- sum(w$domain_index > w$region_mean_jk, na.rm = TRUE); Q$infill_paired <- sum(is.finite(w$domain_index - w$region_mean_jk)); Q$infill_index_minus_sp <- get1(mean(w$domain_index - w$spatial, na.rm = TRUE)) }
# geostatistical comparator
if (!is.null(MBG)) { m <- MBG |> filter(estimand == "infill") |> group_by(target, arm) |> summarise(v = mean(rho_agg, na.rm = TRUE), w = mean(wmae_agg, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  gm <- function(tg, a, col = "v") get1(m[[col]][m$target == tg & m$arm == a])
  Q$mbg_index <- gm("level", "domain_index"); Q$mbg_mbg <- gm("level", "mbg"); Q$mbg_dhs <- gm("level", "mbg_dhs"); Q$mbg_gp <- gm("level", "mbg_gp")
  Q$mbg_index_p <- gm("prev", "domain_index"); Q$mbg_mbg_p <- gm("prev", "mbg"); Q$mbg_w_index <- gm("prev", "domain_index", "w"); Q$mbg_w_mbg <- gm("prev", "mbg", "w")
  w2 <- MBG |> filter(estimand == "infill", target == "level", arm %in% c("domain_index", "mbg")) |> select(country, outcome, arm, rho_agg) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = rho_agg)
  Q$mbg_index_better <- sum(w2$domain_index > w2$mbg, na.rm = TRUE); Q$mbg_cells <- sum(is.finite(w2$domain_index - w2$mbg))
  mr <- MBG |> filter(estimand == "region", target == "level") |> group_by(arm) |> summarise(v = mean(rho_agg, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  Q$mbg_region_index <- get1(mr$v[mr$arm == "domain_index"]); Q$mbg_region_mbg <- get1(mr$v[mr$arm == "mbg"]) }
# weight sources: paired against the index
if (!is.null(WS)) { w <- WS |> filter(estimand == "country", target == "level") |> select(country, outcome, arm, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = spearman)
  pd <- function(a) c(d = get1(mean(w[[a]] - w$domain_index, na.rm = TRUE)), b = sum(w[[a]] > w$domain_index, na.rm = TRUE), n = sum(is.finite(w[[a]] - w$domain_index)))
  Q$ws_decor <- pd("index_decor"); Q$ws_sparse20 <- pd("sparse20"); Q$ws_soft1 <- pd("index_soft1"); Q$ws_enet <- pd("domain_enet"); Q$ws_ridge <- pd("ridge_min")
  wi <- WS |> filter(estimand == "infill", target == "level") |> select(country, outcome, arm, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = spearman)
  pdi <- function(a) get1(mean(wi[[a]] - wi$domain_index, na.rm = TRUE))
  Q$wsi_ridge <- pdi("ridge_min"); Q$wsi_enet <- pdi("domain_enet"); Q$wsi_lasso <- pdi("lasso_min"); Q$wsi_decor <- pdi("index_decor"); Q$wsi_sparse20 <- pdi("sparse20"); Q$wsi_sparse5 <- pdi("sparse5")
  Q$ws_1se_scored <- if (!is.null(WS)) sum(is.finite(WS$spearman[WS$estimand == "country" & WS$target == "level" & WS$arm == "enet_1se"])) else NA }
# targeting
if (!is.null(NTS)) { nt <- NTS |> filter(estimand == "infill"); Q$cap_index <- get1(nt$mean_capture[nt$arm == "domain_index"]); Q$cap_jk <- get1(nt$mean_capture[nt$arm == "region_mean_jk"]); Q$cap_null <- get1(nt$mean_capture[nt$arm == "null_train_mean"]); Q$cap_oracle <- get1(nt$mean_capture[nt$arm == "oracle_ceiling"]) }
# ablation
abl_delta <- function(X, unit) {   # per cell: full-model Spearman (row "ALL") minus the value with the unit dropped
  full <- X |> filter(variant == "full", .data[[unit]] == "ALL") |> select(target, outcome, heldout, full = spearman)
  X |> filter(variant == "drop", .data[[unit]] != "ALL") |> inner_join(full, by = c("target", "outcome", "heldout")) |> mutate(delta = full - spearman)
}
if (!is.null(DA)) { das <- abl_delta(DA, "domain") |> filter(target == "level") |> group_by(domain) |> summarise(delta = mean(delta, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |> arrange(desc(delta))
  Q$da_top <- head(das, 5); Q$da_neg <- sum(das$delta <= 0); Q$da_n <- nrow(das) }
if (!is.null(SA)) { sas <- abl_delta(SA, "source") |> filter(target == "level") |> group_by(source) |> summarise(full = mean(full, na.rm = TRUE), drop = mean(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  Q$sa_dhs_full <- get1(sas$full[sas$source == "DHS"]); Q$sa_dhs_drop <- get1(sas$drop[sas$source == "DHS"]); Q$sa_dhs_cols <- if (is.null(SAS)) NA else get1(SAS$n_cols[SAS$source == "DHS" & SAS$target == "level"])
  im <- grepl("^MICS microdata", sas$source); Q$sa_mics <- get1(sas$full[im] - sas$drop[im]); Q$sa_mics_cols <- if (is.null(SAS)) NA else get1(SAS$n_cols[grepl("^MICS microdata", SAS$source) & SAS$target == "level"]) }
# RR-11 (2026-09-16): the headline set has no DHS; the with-DHS and open-only transport arms are read from their own summaries
BMD <- rd(P2, "benchmarks_v2_summary_withdhs.csv"); BMO <- rd(P2, "benchmarks_v2_summary_open.csv")
bmx <- function(X, est, tg, arm) if (is.null(X)) NA_real_ else get1(X$mean_spearman[X$estimand == est & X$target == tg & X$arm == arm])
Q$tr_dhs <- bmx(BMD, "country", "level", "domain_index"); Q$tr_dhs_p <- bmx(BMD, "country", "prev", "domain_index")
Q$tr_open <- bmx(BMO, "country", "level", "domain_index"); Q$tr_open_p <- bmx(BMO, "country", "prev", "domain_index")
Q$n_dhs <- if (is.null(MD)) NA else sum(MD$source == "DHS"); Q$n_head <- if (is.null(MD) || !"tier" %in% names(MD)) NA else sum(MD$tier %in% c("open", "survey_public") & as.logical(toupper(as.character(MD$subnational))))
# training curve slope
if (!is.null(TC)) { tcm <- TC |> filter(arm == "domain_index", target == "level") |> group_by(n_train_countries) |> summarise(v = mean(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"); Q$tc_slope <- get1((tcm$v[tcm$n_train_countries == 3] - tcm$v[tcm$n_train_countries == 1]) / 2) }
if (!is.null(TCS)) { tcc <- TCS |> filter(set == "climate_soil", target == "level"); Q$tcs_pos1 <- get1(mean(tcc$spearman[tcc$n_train_countries == 1] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)) }
# urbanicity
if (!is.null(UR)) { u <- UR |> filter(target == "level", tier == "admin2"); Q$ur_cs <- mean(u$rho_cs, na.rm = TRUE); Q$ur_partial <- mean(u$partial_cs, na.rm = TRUE); Q$ur_only <- mean(u$rho_urb_only, na.rm = TRUE) }
# ceiling
if (!is.null(VC)) { v <- VC |> filter(rung == "admin2", target == "prev"); Q$vc_honest <- mean(v$ceiling_vc, na.rm = TRUE); Q$vc_split <- mean(v$ceiling_within_vc, na.rm = TRUE); Q$vc_share <- mean(v$cluster_share_of_ceiling, na.rm = TRUE); Q$vc_at <- sum(v$achieved_spearman >= v$ceiling_vc, na.rm = TRUE); Q$vc_n <- sum(is.finite(v$ceiling_vc)) }
# survey design
if (!is.null(AR)) { a <- AR |> filter(rank_from == "prev", set == "climate_soil", fraction == 0.05) |> group_by(design) |> summarise(mae = median(mae, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  Q$ar_a1 <- get1(a$mae[a$design == "A1_anchor_rank"]); Q$ar_c <- get1(a$mae[a$design == "C_regional_survey"]); Q$ar_b <- get1(a$mae[a$design == "B_district_survey"])
  b <- AR |> filter(rank_from == "prev", set == "climate_soil", design == "B_district_survey") |> group_by(fraction) |> summarise(mae = median(mae, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"); Q$ar_b_match <- get1(min(b$fraction[b$mae <= Q$ar_a1])) }
# cluster track
if (!is.null(CV)) { cvm <- CV |> filter(set == "transportable", arm == "domain_index", estimand == "infill", target == "level"); Q$cv_agg <- mean(cvm$rho_agg, na.rm = TRUE); Q$cv_dist <- mean(cvm$rho_district_v2, na.rm = TRUE) }
# risk classes
if (!is.null(RC)) { r <- RC |> filter(scheme == "who_vitA") |> group_by(arm) |> summarise(ex = mean(exact_admin2, na.rm = TRUE), w1 = mean(within1_admin2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"); Q$rc_ex <- get1(r$ex[r$arm == "domain_index"]); Q$rc_w1 <- get1(r$w1[r$arm == "domain_index"]) }
# individual level
if (!is.null(IL)) { i <- IL |> group_by(set) |> summarise(auc = mean(auc, na.rm = TRUE), bs = mean(brier_skill, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"); Q$il_auc_s <- get1(i$auc[i$set == "survey_only"]); Q$il_auc_p <- get1(i$auc[i$set == "proxies_only"]); Q$il_auc_b <- get1(i$auc[i$set == "both"]); Q$il_bs_max <- max(i$bs, na.rm = TRUE); Q$il_cells <- sum(IL$set == "survey_only")
  ir <- IL |> filter(grepl("iron", outcome), set == "survey_only"); Q$il_iron_max <- max(ir$auc, na.rm = TRUE); Q$il_iron_min_top <- get1(sort(ir$auc, decreasing = TRUE)[3]) }
# SuperLearner comparisons (rank loss run: index, rank ensembles, random forest, mse ensembles)
if (!is.null(SLR)) { s <- SLR |> filter(arm %in% c("domain_index", "rank_nnls", "rf", "mse_nnls", "enet")) |> group_by(country, outcome, arm) |> summarise(sp = median(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = sp); s <- s[stats::complete.cases(s), ]   # the cells every arm scored
  sl <- function(a) get1(mean(s[[a]], na.rm = TRUE)); Q$sl_index <- sl("domain_index"); Q$sl_rank <- sl("rank_nnls"); Q$sl_rf <- sl("rf"); Q$sl_mse <- sl("mse_nnls"); Q$sl_enet <- sl("enet"); Q$sl_cells <- nrow(s) }
if (!is.null(SLH)) { s <- SLH |> group_by(country, outcome, arm) |> summarise(sp = median(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |> group_by(arm) |> summarise(v = mean(sp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"); Q$sl_hapc <- get1(s$v[s$arm == "hapc"]) }
# importance shares
if (!is.null(ID)) { e <- ID |> filter(scope == "pooled", target == "level") |> group_by(outcome) |> summarise(env = sum(share[domain %in% c("Satellite embedding", "Climate and weather", "Soil characteristics")]), .groups = "drop"); Q$env_lo <- min(e$env); Q$env_hi <- max(e$env) }
if (!is.null(IT)) { ci20 <- IT |> filter(outcome == "child_iron", target == "level", rank <= 20); Q$ci_rep <- sum(ci20$incountry_sign_agree == ci20$incountry_fits); Q$ci_loco <- sum(ci20$loco_sign_agree == ci20$loco_fits) }

# ---- data-sources deck additions --------------------------------------------------------
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
FIG <- "../../results/figures/policy_deck"; GREY <- "grey65"; BLUE <- "#1f4e79"; LIGHT <- "#6baed6"
source(file.path(root, "R", "predictor_plain_names.R"))   # PLAIN, clean_code()
tier_lab <- c(open = "Open data", survey_public = "Public survey microdata", survey_dhs = "DHS (access agreement)")
tier_col <- c(`Open data` = BLUE, `Public survey microdata` = LIGHT, `DHS (access agreement)` = GREY)

MD  <- rd(root, "data", "covariates", "harmonized", "predictors_admin2_shared_metadata.csv")
AL  <- { f <- sort(list.files(file.path(root, "results", "tables"), pattern = "^predictor_alignment_.*[.]csv$", full.names = TRUE), decreasing = TRUE); if (length(f)) read.csv(f[1], stringsAsFactors = FALSE) else NULL }
SP  <- rd(root, "metadata", "admin2_spine.csv"); SY <- rd(root, "metadata", "survey_years.csv")
EX  <- rd(root, "metadata", "covariates", "exclusions.csv"); OV <- rd(root, "metadata", "covariates", "domain_overrides.csv")
BM  <- rd(P2, "benchmarks_v2_summary.csv"); BMD <- rd(P2, "benchmarks_v2_summary_withdhs.csv"); BMO <- rd(P2, "benchmarks_v2_summary_open.csv")
DA  <- rd(P2, "domain_ablation_loco.csv"); SAS <- rd(P2, "source_ablation_loco_summary.csv"); ND <- rd(P2, "nested_domain_selection.csv")
IT  <- rd(P2, "index_importance_top.csv"); ID <- rd(P2, "index_importance_domains.csv")

source_label <- function(s) dplyr::case_when(
  grepl("^DHS", s) ~ "DHS indicators", grepl("^MICS microdata", s) ~ "MICS microdata", grepl("HEAT", s) ~ "MICS via WHO HEAT",
  grepl("^HCES", s) ~ "Household budget surveys (HCES)", grepl("AlphaEarth", s) ~ "AlphaEarth satellite embedding",
  grepl("SoilGrids", s) ~ "SoilGrids / iSDA soil", grepl("^GEE", s) ~ "Earth Engine: climate, land, built environment",
  grepl("IHME", s) ~ "IHME modelled surfaces", grepl("Malaria Atlas", s) ~ "Malaria Atlas Project", grepl("MapSPAM", s) ~ "MapSPAM crops",
  grepl("Koppen", s) ~ "Koppen / agro-ecological zones", grepl("HFID", s) ~ "HFID food security", grepl("Real-Time Food Prices", s) ~ "World Bank RTFP prices",
  grepl("Tang et al", s) ~ "MIMI dietary inadequacy (Ghana)", grepl("WFP", s) ~ "WFP market prices", grepl("FAOSTAT", s) ~ "FAOSTAT food balance (national)",
  grepl("Livestock", s) ~ "Gridded Livestock of the World", grepl("ESPEN", s) ~ "WHO ESPEN helminths", grepl("Surface Water", s) ~ "Earth Engine: water and coast distance",
  grepl("GFDx", s) ~ "GFDx fortification", grepl("Global Anaemia", s) ~ "WHO anaemia estimates", grepl("Global Data Lab", s) ~ "Global Data Lab HDI",
  grepl("VAS", s) ~ "UNICEF vitamin A supplementation", grepl("FluNet", s) ~ "WHO FluNet", TRUE ~ "WorldPop / GHS / RWI")
if (!is.null(MD)) {
  Q$n <- nrow(MD); Q$n_src <- length(unique(MD$source)); Q$n_open <- sum(MD$tier == "open"); Q$n_pub <- sum(MD$tier == "survey_public"); Q$n_dhs <- sum(MD$tier == "survey_dhs")
  Q$n_const <- sum(!MD$subn); Q$n_head <- sum(MD$tier %in% c("open", "survey_public") & MD$subn)
  Q$n_static <- sum(is.na(MD$year_offset_max_abs)); Q$n_exact <- sum(MD$year_offset_max_abs == 0, na.rm = TRUE); Q$n_off3 <- sum(MD$year_offset_max_abs >= 3, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q$n_modelled <- sum(as.logical(toupper(as.character(MD$modelled_surface))), na.rm = TRUE)
}
if (!is.null(RV)) { rv <- RV[RV$tiers == "open+survey_public+survey_dhs", ]; Q$n_common <- get1(as.numeric(rv[["transport common"]] %||% rv$transport_common)); Q$n_declared <- get1(as.numeric(rv$declared)) }
Q$n_assembled <- 614   # columns before the exclusion rules, from the 15 September full rebuild (logs/tail_53.log: 614 -> 570)
# columns that were built and then removed by an exclusion rule: the union of every backup and block
# metadata file on disk, matched against metadata/covariates/exclusions.csv (built = in the set + excluded)
built_excluded <- function() {
  if (is.null(MD) || is.null(EX)) return(NULL)
  HD <- file.path(root, "data", "covariates", "harmonized")
  fs <- c(list.files(HD, pattern = "^predictors_admin2_shared_metadata[.]csv[.]pre_", full.names = TRUE), list.files(HD, pattern = "^predictors_admin2_[a-z_]+_metadata[.]csv$", full.names = TRUE))
  u <- MD[, c("column", "source")]
  for (f in fs) { m <- tryCatch(read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL); if (!is.null(m) && all(c("column", "source") %in% names(m))) u <- rbind(u, m[!m$column %in% u$column, c("column", "source")]) }
  u <- u[!duplicated(u$column), ]; gone <- u[!u$column %in% MD$column, ]
  hit <- vapply(gone$column, function(cc) any(vapply(EX$canonical_regex, function(rx) grepl(rx, cc, perl = TRUE), NA)), NA)
  gone[hit, ]
}
BX <- built_excluded()
# predictors that recur in the top twenty of the leave-one-country-out fits (script 57, scope "loco", biomarker level)
IC <- rd(P2, "index_importance_columns.csv")
REC <- if (is.null(IC)) NULL else IC |> filter(scope == "loco", target == "level", rank <= 20) |> group_by(column, domain) |>
  summarise(n_fits = n(), n_outcomes = n_distinct(outcome), sign_agree = max(mean(beta_std > 0), mean(beta_std < 0)), mean_w = mean(beta_std), .groups = "drop") |> arrange(desc(n_fits), desc(sign_agree))
Q$loco_fits <- if (is.null(IC)) 22 else nrow(distinct(IC |> filter(scope == "loco", target == "level"), fit, outcome))
rec1 <- function(col, what = "n_fits") if (is.null(REC) || !col %in% REC$column) NA else REC[[what]][REC$column == col]
# quantities the concept slides (the YAML) read
if (!is.null(NTS)) { nt <- NTS[NTS$estimand == "infill", ]; g1 <- function(a, col) get1(nt[[col]][nt$arm == a])
  Q$top20_prev_index <- g1("domain_index", "mean_prev_top20"); Q$top20_prev_nat <- g1("domain_index", "mean_prev_national")
  Q$top20_prev_oracle <- g1("oracle_ceiling", "mean_prev_top20"); Q$cap_oracle <- g1("oracle_ceiling", "mean_capture"); Q$lift_index <- g1("domain_index", "mean_lift") }
# share of district pairs the held-out prediction orders the same way as the survey: counted exactly by

if (!is.null(NTS) && "mean_concordance" %in% names(NTS)) { gc <- function(est, a) get1(NTS$mean_concordance[NTS$estimand == est & NTS$arm == a])
  Q$pairs_pct <- gc("infill", "domain_index"); Q$pairs_jk <- gc("infill", "region_mean_jk"); Q$pairs_sp <- gc("infill", "spatial"); Q$pairs_pct_tr <- gc("country", "domain_index")
  Q$pairs_tr_cells <- get1(NTS$cells[NTS$estimand == "country" & NTS$arm == "domain_index"]) }
Q$ceiling_share <- Q$infill_index_p / Q$vc_honest              # prevalence target against the honest ceiling on the same target
if (!is.null(RC)) { r <- RC |> filter(scheme == "who_vitA") |> group_by(arm) |> summarise(ex = mean(exact_admin2, na.rm = TRUE), w1 = mean(within1_admin2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  Q$rc_jk_ex <- get1(r$ex[r$arm == "region_mean_jk"]); Q$rc_jk_w1 <- get1(r$w1[r$arm == "region_mean_jk"]); Q$rc_sp_ex <- get1(r$ex[r$arm == "spatial"])
  Q$rc_far <- 1 - Q$rc_w1; Q$rc_jk_far <- 1 - Q$rc_jk_w1 }
Q$n_spine <- if (is.null(SP)) NA else nrow(SP)
Q$rec_ruminant <- rec1("glw_ruminant_share"); Q$rec_staple <- rec1("fprice_staple_rel"); Q$rec_staple_outcomes <- rec1("fprice_staple_rel", "n_outcomes")
```

## Goals

::: {.notes}
The three project goals as stated in the proposal: district and national prevalence estimates from proxies, validated against biomarker surveys; the districts at greatest risk; engagement with national stakeholders throughout. The map is Ghana child iron deficiency from the 2017 survey, the worked example that recurs through the talk.
:::

## Motivation

::: {.notes}
Photo credit: Latter-day Saint Charities. GMS 2017 collaborators: University of Ghana, GroundWork, University of Wisconsin-Madison, KEMRI-Wellcome Trust; with UNICEF and Global Affairs Canada.
:::

## Big data and small data, at once

::: {.notes}
The same sentence describes both halves. Big: `r Q$n_pred` columns from `r Q$n_src` sources, most of them rasters at 30 m to 10 km summarised over `r nrow(SP)` districts, four household surveys aggregated from their microdata, a satellite embedding with 64 dimensions per district. Small: the thing being predicted is measured in one biomarker survey per country per decade, at `r Q$n_districts` surveyed districts over four countries, `r Q$n_cells` country-outcome cells, and 14 to 87 districts per country, which is the effective sample size of every model. Everything in the protocol follows from holding both at once: predictors are reduced to domain components with nothing chosen on the outcome, the estimator has no tuned parameter, the folds are cut by district, region and country, and the reliability ceiling says how much of the survey signal is noise at district level. Likely question: why not fit at the person level. That was the January approach; a person-level classifier under district-blocked folds is a coin toss on proxies alone, and shrinking its predictions biases area means (individual-level slide in the appendix).
:::

# Surveys and outcomes

## The four surveys

::: {.notes}
`r Q$n_cells` country-outcome cells, `r Q$n_districts` surveyed districts, `r Q$n_clusters` survey clusters with GPS. Fieldwork dates were recovered for every cluster (Sierra Leone reconstructed from date of birth and age in days); ferritin, retinol and food prices are seasonal. Three surveys ran in the dry season and Malawi in the lean season. Likely question: why districts rather than regions. Districts are the programme unit; they sit below the surveys' design resolution, so the reliability ceiling slide reports what a perfect predictor could reach.
:::

## Outcomes

::: {.notes}
Two targets per cell: the deficiency prevalence, and the district mean of the negated log biomarker concentration (higher means worse), which carries more signal than the dichotomy and is reported alongside it. Definitions were reconciled against the four survey reports and the 21 papers that re-analyse them on 15 September 2026 (docs/survey_report_reconciliation.md): every iron, zinc, folate and B12 national estimate now reproduces its report to the decimal, and the Gambia LGA estimates track the report at r = 0.98 to 0.99. What changed then: the iron binaries had been the surveys' iron-deficiency-ANAEMIA columns in three countries (ferritin plus haemoglobin), Malawi's iron flag came from a mis-specified local BRINDA that under-counted by half, pregnant women and children outside 6 to 59 months were being kept, and vitamin A had been converted to retinol-equivalents with each survey's own RBP-to-retinol line. That conversion is now the sensitivity analysis, not the primary: the four lines were fitted in different directions on 14 to 300 specimens, and Malawi's has R-squared 0.13, which manufactures near-zero deficiency by construction; the survey's own re-analysis (Likoswe 2021) recommends exactly BRINDA-adjusted RBP below 0.70, the estimand used here. Call it low RBP rather than vitamin A deficiency: Ghana's MRDR found 6.7 percent depleted and Malawi's none. Two caveats to say if asked. Sierra Leone's child file as supplied holds only the survey's anaemic children (532 of 654 assayed), so its child cells are anaemic-subgroup estimates until the full file arrives. Folate is not comparable across the two assays (Malawi's microbiologic assay reads higher than the Roche immunoassay), so its cross-border numbers are indicative only. Iodine (The Gambia, Sierra Leone) is analysed within country only; a one- or two-country outcome has no cross-border test.
:::

# The proxy dataset

## What a proxy has to be

::: {.notes}
This talk is about the right-hand side of the model: where the `r Q$n` columns come from, how each one gets from its native form to a district value, how we line them up with four surveys taken in four different years, and which of them the model leans on. The analysis deck covers what the ranking achieves; this one covers what it is made of. The leakage rule is the second bullet: a district aggregate of the same survey instance we score is excluded (docs/findings, LK-02), and where a MICS or DHS was fielded inside the biomarker survey's own clusters those clusters are dropped from the aggregate (The Gambia 2018: 70 MICS clusters; Malawi 2015-16: 105 DHS clusters). The record behind the fourth bullet is the shared metadata file and results/tables/protocol_v2/variable_sheet.csv. One consequence of the first bullet: `r Q$n_const` of the `r Q$n` columns are national series with one value per country, and a value that is the same in every district cannot rank districts, so the models drop them when they are fitted.
:::

## What each source is (1 of 2): land, climate, agriculture

```{r source-table-1}
kb(df(Source = c("Earth Engine: TerraClimate", "Earth Engine: MODIS", "Earth Engine: land cover, lights, built-up", "Earth Engine: productivity", "AlphaEarth", "SoilGrids / iSDA", "Koppen / AEZ", "JRC Surface Water / LSIB", "MapSPAM", "Gridded Livestock of the World", "WorldPop / GHSL / GPW / RWI"),
  `What it is` = c("Monthly climate (rain, temperature, evapotranspiration, soil moisture), 4 km; survey year and 1991-2020 normals", "Land-surface temperature (1 km), NDVI and EVI (250 m) at the survey year, plus climatology and anomaly", "Copernicus land-cover fractions, night lights, GHSL built-up surface, human modification", "MODIS NPP and GPP, WaPOR evapotranspiration, leaf area, grassland cover", "Google's 64-number satellite embedding of a year of imagery, 10 m, 2017", "Soil nutrients at two depths, pH, texture, organic carbon (iSDA 30 m, SoilGrids 250 m)", "Climate classes and agro-ecological zones: class shares and purity", "Distance to permanent and seasonal water and to the coast", "Crop area and production by crop, 10 km, 2010", "Cattle, sheep, goats, pigs and poultry per km2, 10 km, 2015", "Population, age-sex structure and density; Meta's relative wealth index")), digits = 0)
```

## The sources

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
`r Q$n` columns from `r Q$n_src` sources, harmonised onto one district spine. `r if (!is.null(MD)) sum(MD$n_countries == 4) else 510` exist in all four countries and can serve a model for a new country; the other `r if (!is.null(MD)) sum(MD$n_countries < 4) else 60` exist in one to three and are used inside the countries that have them.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r sources, fig.width=6.2, fig.height=5.4, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(MD)) {
  d <- df(Source = source_label(MD$source), Coverage = ifelse(MD$n_countries == 4, "In all four countries", "In one to three countries")) |> count(Source, Coverage, name = "n")
  tot <- tapply(d$n, d$Source, sum); d$Source <- factor(d$Source, levels = names(sort(tot))); d$Coverage <- factor(d$Coverage, levels = c("In all four countries", "In one to three countries"))
  ggplot(d, aes(n, Source, fill = Coverage)) + geom_col(width = 0.72, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
    geom_text(data = df(Source = factor(names(tot), levels = levels(d$Source)), n = as.vector(tot)), aes(n, Source, label = n), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = -0.2, size = 3.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`In all four countries` = BLUE, `In one to three countries` = LIGHT)) + scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
    labs(x = "Columns in the harmonised set (label = total)", y = NULL, fill = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") + guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Read the bar chart from the top. One harmonised set feeds every model: the in-country models use whatever a country has, the cross-country models the columns all four share, so the light segment (household budget survey diet items for two countries, RTFP prices for two, MIMI for Ghana, MICS items missing from one round, a few IHME surfaces) works at home and not abroad. Behind the set sits a larger extraction: about 740 columns per country in the raw files (1,968 distinct names across the four, mostly the same quantity under country-specific names), harmonised to a common vocabulary; what did not harmonise was used only in the pre-protocol models. The Earth Engine block is climate (TerraClimate at the survey year and as 30-year normals), land cover, night lights, built-up surface, vegetation and evapotranspiration, night-time land surface temperature; the satellite embedding is Google's AlphaEarth, 64 numbers per district that summarise a year of imagery; soil is iSDA and SoilGrids, ten nutrient concentrations at two depths plus texture and pH; crops are MapSPAM's 2010 allocation; livestock is GLW4. The health and nutrition surfaces are IHME's modelled estimates (anaemia, child growth, WASH, education, ORS, HIV, malaria, vaccination) and the Malaria Atlas layers; ESPEN gives helminth endemicity. Prices come from WFP markets, the World Bank's RTFP panel and FAOSTAT balances; fortification from GFDx. The public microdata blocks are new since 15 September: 30 indicators from the MICS files for all four countries and 15 diet and consumption indicators from the household budget surveys (IHS 2015/16, GLSS7, IHS4, SLIHS 2018). The DHS block is 150 district aggregates from the round paired with each survey (Ghana 2014, Malawi 2015-16, Sierra Leone 2013, The Gambia 2019-20), estimated with a cluster-level spatial model so every district has a value. Everything here is listed with its source, year and definition in results/tables/protocol_v2/variable_sheet.csv and in the dashboard's catalogue.
:::

## Three kinds of data, three ways to a district value

```{r aggregation}
kb(df(`Native form` = c("Gridded raster (30 m to 10 km)", "Survey with GPS clusters", "Survey identified to region or district", "National series"),
  Examples = c("Climate, soil, satellite, IHME and MAP surfaces, population", "DHS; MICS 2018 in The Gambia, 2017 in Sierra Leone", "MICS in Ghana and Malawi; household budget surveys", "FAOSTAT balances, GFDx programme fields, FluNet"),
  `To a district` = c("Zonal mean over the district polygon, area- or population-weighted", "DHS: cluster spatial model (BYM2) so every district has a value; MICS: clusters inside the polygon, minimum 30 households", "Value of the smallest survey unit that contains the district, flagged as the parent's value", "Constant within a country; dropped when the model is fitted"),
  `Time` = c("Survey year, nearest year, or 30-year normal plus anomaly", "The round paired with the biomarker survey", "The round nearest the survey", "Survey year")), digits = 0)
```

::: {.notes}
Rasters are the easy case: exactextractr over the GADM polygon, weighting by WorldPop where the quantity is about people (the IHME surfaces) and by area where it is about land (climate, soil, greenness). Twelve of the IHME columns were still joined by district name until this week; the tabular files predate Ghana's 2019 district splits and left 56 percent of Ghana empty, so they were re-extracted from the 5 km GeoTIFFs. Survey microdata with GPS goes point-in-polygon after the leakage clusters are removed, with a minimum of 30 households and 5 clusters per district before a district gets its own value; below that it takes the parent region's value and is flagged. Ghana's MICS 2017-18 identifies the ten old regions and Malawi's MICS 2013-14 the 27 districts, so those blocks vary at that level only and every column carries a subnational flag saying so. National series are kept in the set for documentation and completeness, but a constant cannot rank districts; the fit-time policy removes `r Q$n_const` of them (FAOSTAT, most GFDx fields, WHO anaemia national estimates, VAS, FluNet).
:::

## Linking in space: one spine, coded keys

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- `r nrow(SP)` districts on GADM 4.1: `r paste(sprintf("%s %d", sub("SierraLeone", "Sierra Leone", names(table(SP$country))), as.vector(table(SP$country))), collapse = ", ")`.
- Every unit carries its GADM code, HASC code and the OCHA p-code, so a join is by code where the source has one.
- Names are matched only as a last resort, through a reviewed alias table with a distance cap, and always on the region-district pair: Malawi has four Traditional Authority names that occur in two districts.
- A join that fans out or drops a unit fails the build. The population table had been missing one of each same-name pair for months; the test found it.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Ghana: 260 districts on the 2019 boundaries; sources on the 2012 boundaries (216) or the ten old regions are mapped with a crosswalk, never by name.
- Malawi: `r sum(SP$country == "Malawi")` Traditional Authorities; sources at district level (28) are broadcast down and flagged.
- The Gambia: 37 districts; Sierra Leone: 14 districts. With so few units, a fallback to the parent region changes more of the map.
- Survey clusters are linked to the same polygons for the cluster-level analyses and buffered for raster extraction.
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
The spine is metadata/admin2_spine.csv; the helpers in R/admin2_keys.R do every join in the pipeline and a lint test (tests/testthat/test-admin2-join-lint.R) reads every script for a join on a bare Admin2 name. The p-codes came from OCHA's COD-AB for all four countries this week, both directions, so an OCHA-coded source (IPC, ACLED, cluster surveys) joins without any matching. Fuzzy matching, where it is still needed, is Jaro-Winkler with a 0.15 cap and a review file that lists every non-exact match for a human to accept. The population defect: the dashboard's population table had been deduplicated by district name, so Chikwawa's TA Lundu and Nsanje's TA Ngabu, Salima's TA Pemba and Zomba's TA Malemia lost one member each, two of them surveyed districts, and every population-weighted figure silently excluded them. Fixed 15 September from WorldPop density, and the population table is now asserted complete in the tests.
:::

## Linking in time: four surveys, four years

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Surveys: The Gambia 2018, Ghana 2017, Malawi 2016, Sierra Leone 2013. Each column is placed by a written rule and stamped with the year used and the gap. `r Q$n_exact` columns sit on the survey year in every country and `r Q$n_static` are static layers. `r Q$n_off3` are three or more years off in at least one country: the DHS round paired with Ghana's 2017 survey is from 2014, Sierra Leone's 2013 survey predates the satellite embedding and its nearest MICS by four years, and MapSPAM's 2010 crop map is the oldest layer everywhere.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r time, fig.width=6.2, fig.height=4.4, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(AL)) {
  a <- AL |> filter(has_data) |> mutate(gap = case_when(is.na(year_offset) ~ "Static layer", abs(year_offset) == 0 ~ "Survey year", abs(year_offset) <= 2 ~ "1 to 2 years off", abs(year_offset) <= 4 ~ "3 to 4 years off", TRUE ~ "5 or more years off"),
    gap = factor(gap, levels = c("Survey year", "1 to 2 years off", "3 to 4 years off", "5 or more years off", "Static layer")), country = sub("^Gambia$", "The Gambia", sub("SierraLeone", "Sierra Leone", country))) |>
    count(country, gap) |> group_by(country) |> mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |> ungroup()
  ggplot(a, aes(share, country, fill = gap)) + geom_col(width = 0.7, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) + scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Survey year` = BLUE, `1 to 2 years off` = LIGHT, `3 to 4 years off` = "#fdae61", `5 or more years off` = "#d7191c", `Static layer` = "grey75")) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + labs(x = "Share of columns with a value in the country", y = NULL, fill = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) + guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
The rules live in metadata/covariates/temporal_alignment.csv, `r if (!is.null(AL)) length(unique(AL$rule_id)) else 45` of them, one regular expression each: survey_year where an annual series exists (TerraClimate, MODIS NDVI, MAP, WorldPop density, WFP prices, RTFP windows), nearest available year where a series ends early (IHME's child growth, education and WASH stop at 2017, anaemia and malaria at 2019), a fixed vintage where there is only one (AlphaEarth 2017, MapSPAM 2010, GLW 2015, RWI 2019), a per-country round for the household surveys, and static for soil, terrain, climate normals and zones. Climate and greenness enter as a 30-year normal plus the survey-year anomaly in standard-deviation units, which is what transports; the calendar-year series that lagged the survey by up to eight years were retired. Sierra Leone's 2013 survey is the awkward one: AlphaEarth starts in 2017, Copernicus land cover in 2015, and the MICS round nearest it is 2017, so its gaps are the orange and red bands. Ghana's are the DHS block: the round paired with the 2017 survey is the 2014 DHS, three years off for 140 columns. The gaps that apply everywhere are the single-vintage products: MapSPAM 2010, GLW 2015, WorldPop's 2020 age-sex structure. The stamp is per column and per country (results/tables/predictor_alignment_2026-09-16.csv), and the audit lists everything three or more years off.
:::

## Predictor domains

::: {.notes}
Why domains: `r Q$n` columns against 14 to 87 districts per country cannot be fitted column by column, and the columns are heavily correlated within a source. Grouping them by what they measure and taking principal components inside each group keeps most of the variance of each group, treats a source with 64 columns and a source with 3 as one construct each, and keeps the outcome out of the representation: the rotations are learned from the training districts' predictors alone, so nothing is selected on the biomarker. The grouping is written down: each source block brings a label, and `r if (!is.null(OV)) nrow(OV) else 10` override rules in metadata/covariates/domain_overrides.csv regroup columns by construct (infection and inflammation burden, immunisation, anaemia, child anthropometry, infant feeding, supplementation, water and sanitation, education, child mortality, assets), so that MAP, IHME, DHS and MICS versions of the same thing are weighed together. Two things went wrong this week and are now guarded. A domain's first twelve characters are its key inside the model; two labels that shared them ("Food prices (RTFP)" and "Food prices and supply") were silently merged in two analyses until a check caught it on 16 September. The other is in the exclusions, on the next slide. One more point for questions: climate alone or soil alone transports better than all domains together, the analysis deck's climate-and-soil result.
:::

## Data assembly

::: {.notes}
Six steps from four surveys and `r Q$n_src` sources to one district table. The CONSORT table on the next slide gives the column counts at each step.
:::

## Building the harmonised dataset

```{r pipeline}
kb(df(Step = c("Assemble", "Append blocks", "Exclude", "Stamp", "Fit-time policy", "Transport matrix"),
  `What happens` = c("Base extraction on the spine, food environment, extra sources, add-back sources", "Household budget surveys, MICS microdata, RTFP prices, MODIS NDVI, climate normals", "Rules with a written reason: data defects, superseded layers, redundant twins", "Access tier, within-country variation, alignment rule, year used and gap, modelled-surface flag", "Drop national constants and leakage columns", "Per country: coverage of at least 70% and some variation; then the four-country intersection"),
  Columns = c("", as.character(Q$n_assembled), as.character(Q$n), as.character(Q$n), as.character(Q$n_declared %||% 525), as.character(Q$n_common %||% 464))), digits = 0)
```

::: {.notes}
One shell script runs the chain (scripts/covariates/rebuild_shared_tail.sh) and ends in an audit that fails the build on a domain-key collision, a column declared subnational that does not vary, or a join that fans out. The exclusion file has `r if (!is.null(EX)) nrow(EX) else 22` rules and every rule states its evidence: a nitrogen layer whose medians differ thirtyfold between countries, an NDVI product declared available only to 2013, calendar-year series superseded by survey-year values. This week's most instructive mistake was in the exclusions. A review labelled the soil dispersion bands and the 20-50 cm depth means "redundant" on a mechanistic argument, and the climate-and-soil result fell from 0.37 to 0.34 across districts and from 0.45 to 0.40 across regions. The bands correlate only 0.03 to 0.69 with the depth means, so the label was wrong; restoring them brought both numbers back. We now hold to one rule: nothing is added or regrouped because a score likes it, an exclusion whose stated premise fails on its own metric is reverted, and every set change is checked against the transport arms before a run. What a model can see is the last two rows: `r Q$n_declared %||% 525` columns vary within a country, of which `r Q$n_common %||% 464` have a value in all four countries and so can be used to predict a new one. The rest are per-country data gaps: household budget diet indicators pending for Ghana and Sierra Leone, RTFP for The Gambia and Malawi only, MICS items absent from one round.
:::

# Models and protocol

## Estimators

::: {.notes}
On the same folds the index scores `r f2(Q$sl_index)` against `r f2(Q$sl_rank)` for the rank-loss ensemble, `r f2(Q$sl_rf)` for random forest, `r f2(Q$sl_mse)` for the squared-error ensemble, `r f2(Q$sl_hapc)` for the principal-component highly adaptive ridge and `r f2(Q$sl_enet)` for the elastic net (mean of cell medians over the `r Q$sl_cells` cells every arm scored, prevalence, in-fill; SL-01 to SL-05, rerun on the RR-10 set). Likely question: why capacity hurts. With 14 to 87 districts per country the index has no tuned parameter, and every estimator that tunes one shrinks toward the constant under squared-error cross-validation; the weighting slide quantifies this over a family of penalties.
:::

## Ensemble machine learning

::: {.notes}
The January estimator, kept as the comparison arm: a SuperLearner library (mean, penalised regressions, random forest, gradient boosting, PCA-HAL, BART, geostatistical models) weighted by V-fold cross-validated performance, folds cut so that no district is split between training and validation. No penalty other than computation to add a learner: diversity, redundancy, synergy. On the same folds the index scores `r f2(Q$sl_index)` against `r f2(Q$sl_rank)` for the rank-loss ensemble and `r f2(Q$sl_rf)` for random forest (`r Q$sl_cells` cells, prevalence, in-fill), which is why the zero-tuning index became the headline: with 14 to 87 districts every estimator that tunes a parameter shrinks toward the constant.
:::

## How the zero-tuning index works

::: {.notes}
Four steps, none of which looks at a held-out district. (1) Rank-normalise every predictor within country, so a level offset between surveys cannot act as signal. (2) Take the leading principal components of each of the `r Q$n_dom` domains, to 80% of variance and at most twelve, on the training districts. (3) Weight each component by its rank correlation with the outcome in the training fold, sign and size; nothing else is fitted. (4) Sum, and rescale to the training outcome spread. The index is the infinite-penalty limit of a ridge regression on the components (weighting slide in the appendix), and because it is linear in the rank-normalised columns every column has an exact back-projected weight, which is what the importance slides show.
:::

## Estimands

::: {.notes}
The earlier leaderboard scored transport-style models against an in-fill baseline that read the held-out district's own respondents; that comparison is withdrawn. Counts of positive cells have a fat null when a country's outcomes are correlated: with no transport at all, `r Q$null_pos95` of `r Q$tr_cells` cells are positive at the 95th percentile of the permutation null, so the mean rank correlation is the statistic compared with its null (`r f2(Q$null_d)` at district level, `r f2(Q$null_a1)` at regional level).
:::

# Results

## In-fill: district ranking accuracy

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Mean Spearman correlation over the scored cells with a 95% interval across cells. The index reaches `r f2(Q$infill_index)` on the biomarker level against `r f2(Q$infill_jk)` for the jackknifed regional mean (better in `r Q$infill_beats_jk` of `r Q$infill_paired` cells) and `r f2(Q$infill_sp)` for the covariate-free smoother.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r infill, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(BC)) {
  d <- BC |> filter(estimand == "infill", arm %in% names(arm_label)) |> cell_ci("spearman", c("target", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(arm_label[arm], levels = rev(arm_label)), Target = tlab[target])
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "Target", null = 0, base = 15)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Cells: `r Q$infill_paired` on the level (Sierra Leone's cells score NA at 14 districts). On prevalence the index scores `r f2(Q$infill_index_p)` against `r f2(Q$infill_jk_p)`. The smoother with covariates fitted to its residuals scores `r f2(Q$infill_spd)`; covariates add `r sgn(Q$infill_index_minus_sp)` over the smoother alone on the level. The penalised fits score `r f2(Q$infill_enet)` (domain components) and `r f2(Q$infill_raw)` (all columns). Likely question: why the smoother does so well. Inside a surveyed country the covariates mostly reproduce a smooth surface that neighbouring districts already provide; the value of the covariates is in unsurveyed regions and countries.
:::

## Ghana: survey and held-out prediction

```{r ghana-maps, fig.width=11, fig.height=5.6, dpi=130}
ok <- FALSE
try({
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(sf))
  source(file.path(root, "R", "protocol_v2.R"))
  S  <- read.csv(file.path(root, "data", "covariates", "harmonized", "predictors_admin2_shared.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
  PREDS <- intersect(MD$column, names(S)); domain_of <- stats::setNames(MD$domain, MD$column)
  B <- readRDS(file.path(root, "dashboard", "data", "admin2_boundaries.rds"))[["ghana"]]
  maps <- list()
  for (on in c("child_vitA", "women_iron")) {
    t <- TG[TG$country == "Ghana" & TG$outcome == on & is.finite(TG$y_prev) & is.finite(TG$n_eff), ]
    m <- dplyr::inner_join(t, S[S$country == "Ghana", c("Admin1", "Admin2", PREDS)], by = c("Admin1", "Admin2"))
    Xr <- prep_predictors_v2(as.matrix(m[, PREDS])); Y <- .v2_logit(m$y_prev); aux <- list(Admin1 = m$Admin1, y_nat = Y)
    pred <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(m), 10)
    for (r in 1:10) { folds <- make_folds_v2("kfold_district", nrow(m), k = 5, rep_id = r)
      for (f in unique(folds)) { te <- which(folds == f); tr <- which(folds != f); D <- domain_representation_v2(Xr, domain_of, sign_rows = tr)
        pred[te, r] <- ARMS_V2[["domain_index"]](tr, te, Y, NULL, D, aux) } }
    m$pred <- .v2_expit(rowMeans(pred, na.rm = TRUE)); rho <- cor(m$y_prev, m$pred, method = "spearman")
    g <- dplyr::left_join(B, m[, c("Admin1", "Admin2", "y_prev", "pred")], by = c("Admin1", "Admin2"))
    lab <- if (on == "child_vitA") "Child vitamin A deficiency" else "Women's iron deficiency"
    p1 <- "Survey 2017"; p2 <- sprintf("Held-out index prediction (rho = %.2f)", rho)
    long <- rbind(data.frame(g[, c("Admin1", "Admin2")], value = g$y_prev, panel = p1), data.frame(g[, c("Admin1", "Admin2")], value = g$pred, panel = p2))
    long$panel <- factor(long$panel, levels = c(p1, p2))
    maps[[on]] <- ggplot(sf::st_as_sf(long)) + geom_sf(aes(fill = value), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) + facet_wrap(~ panel) +
      scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = scales::percent, na.value = "grey92", name = NULL) + labs(title = lab) + theme_void(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "right", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  }
  print(patchwork::wrap_plots(maps, ncol = 2)); ok <- TRUE
}, silent = TRUE)
if (!ok) cat("Maps could not be rendered in this session; see the dashboard.")
```

::: {.notes}
Districts with survey data only (grey: no survey clusters). Each district's prediction is made with that district held out (5-fold, averaged over ten draws). The model orders districts; the survey's own estimate at a single-cluster district is itself noisy, which is what the reliability ceiling slide quantifies.
:::

## Region extrapolation

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Leave-one-region-out, mean over cells with a 95% interval. The index scores `r f2(Q$region_index)` on the level and `r f2(Q$region_index_p)` on prevalence; the penalised fits fall to `r f2(Q$region_enet_p)` and `r f2(Q$region_raw_p)` on prevalence.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r region, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(BC)) {
  d <- BC |> filter(estimand == "region", arm %in% names(arm_label)) |> cell_ci("spearman", c("target", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(arm_label[arm], levels = rev(arm_label)), Target = tlab[target])
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "Target", null = 0, base = 15)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Leaving out a whole region is where a smoother must extrapolate past the edge of its data. The index and the smoother stay close (`r f2(Q$region_index)` against `r f2(Q$region_sp)` on the level); the null training mean collapses. Ghana and Malawi are the countries where this estimand is well determined; The Gambia and Sierra Leone give one number per region.
:::

## Country transport

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Leave-one-country-out, `r Q$tr_cells` cells. The full index scores `r f2(Q$tr_index)` at district level (positive in `r Q$tr_index_pos` of `r Q$tr_cells`) and `r f2(Q$tr_a1)` at regional level; the climate-and-soil index scores `r f2(Q$cs_d)` and `r f2(Q$cs_a1)`. Dashed lines are the 95th percentile of the permutation null.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r transport, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(BC) && !is.null(A1) && !is.null(ND) && !is.null(CS1)) {
  d <- bind_rows(
    BC |> filter(estimand == "country", arm %in% c("domain_index", "domain_enet")) |> transmute(tier = "District", target, model = arm_label[arm], spearman),
    ND |> filter(arm == "fixed_cs") |> transmute(tier = "District", target, model = "Climate + soil index", spearman),
    A1 |> filter(arm == "domain_index") |> transmute(tier = "Regional", target, model = arm_label["domain_index"], spearman),
    CS1 |> filter(set == "climate_soil") |> transmute(tier = "Regional", target, model = "Climate + soil index", spearman)) |>
    cell_ci("spearman", c("tier", "target", "model")) |>
    mutate(Target = tlab[target], row = factor(paste(tier, model, sep = ": "), levels = rev(c("District: Zero-tuning domain index", "District: Elastic net, domain components", "District: Climate + soil index", "Regional: Zero-tuning domain index", "Regional: Climate + soil index"))))
  nulls <- df(tier = c("District", "Regional"), null = c(Q$null_d, Q$null_a1))
  ggplot(d, aes(est, row)) + geom_vline(data = nulls, aes(xintercept = null), linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.25, colour = "grey35", orientation = "y") + geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#1f4e79") +
    facet_wrap(~ Target) + labs(x = "Spearman in the held-out country (mean, 95% interval)", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Absolute levels do not transport: raw ferritin differs several-fold between surveys, so the transported product is a ranking. Prevalence: `r f2(Q$tr_index_p)` at district level (`r Q$tr_index_pos_p` of `r Q$tr_cells` positive) and `r f2(Q$tr_a1_p)` at regional level for the full index; `r f2(Q$cs_d_p)` at district level for climate and soil. The climate-and-soil pair was chosen on these four countries, so it enters the next country as a pre-registered prediction; honest nested selection of domains inside the training fold gives a median difference of `r sgn(Q$nested_vs_full)` from the full index (better in `r Q$nested_better` of `r Q$tr_cells`). Since 9 September the DHS-derived predictors are cluster-level spatial estimates at every district (DS-01), which changed nothing in-country and cost the full index 0.01 across borders. Likely question: what a correlation of `r f2(Q$tr_index)` means for a programme. The targeting slide answers in burden captured.
:::

## Geostatistical comparator

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
The DHS Program's model-based geostatistics fitted at the survey clusters (a spatial field plus covariates), scored on the same district folds. On the level it scores `r f2(Q$mbg_mbg)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_index)` for the index (index better in `r Q$mbg_index_better` of `r Q$mbg_cells` cells); on prevalence `r f2(Q$mbg_mbg_p)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_index_p)`.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r geostat, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(MBG)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Zero-tuning domain index", mbg = "Geostatistical, field + domain covariates", mbg_dhs = "Geostatistical, field + DHS covariate list", mbg_gp = "Geostatistical, field only", spatial = "Spatial smoother", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean")
  d <- MBG |> filter(estimand %in% c("infill", "region"), arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("rho_agg", c("estimand", "target", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)), panel = paste(c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region")[estimand], tlab[target], sep = ", "))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "panel", null = 0, base = 12, xlab = "Spearman across districts (mean, 95% interval)")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
INLA-SPDE Matern field with penalised-complexity priors, binomial on cluster counts for prevalence and Gaussian for the level, cluster predictions aggregated to districts by effective sample size; run with the first component of every covariate domain and with the DHS Program's ten-raster list (`r f2(Q$mbg_dhs)` on the level). The field alone scores `r f2(Q$mbg_gp)`. The geostatistical model has the lower absolute error on prevalence (`r f2(Q$mbg_w_mbg, 1)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_w_index, 1)` percentage points) because it estimates a level and shrinks toward it. Under region extrapolation the index scores `r f2(Q$mbg_region_index)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_region_mbg)`. The method needs measured clusters inside the country it predicts, so it has no country-transport estimand. Likely question: whether the two are complementary. Yes: the geostatistical model for a calibrated prevalence where a survey exists, the index for a ranking where none does.
:::

## Targeting value

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Share of the national deficiency burden in the fifth of districts each method ranks worst, in-fill, mean over cells with a 95% interval. The index reaches `r pc(Q$cap_index)`, the jackknifed regional mean `r pc(Q$cap_jk)`, no information `r pc(Q$cap_null)` and perfect knowledge `r pc(Q$cap_oracle)`.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r burden, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(NT)) {
  lab <- c(oracle_ceiling = "Perfect knowledge", domain_index = "Zero-tuning domain index", spatial_plus_domain = "Spatial smoother + covariates", spatial = "Spatial smoother", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean", null_train_mean = "No information")
  d <- NT |> filter(estimand == "infill", arm %in% names(lab)) |> group_by(country, outcome, arm) |> summarise(v = mean(capture_top20, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    cell_ci("v", "arm") |> mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)))
  forest(d, "Model", null = 0.2, base = 14, xlab = "Burden in the worst-ranked fifth (mean, 95% interval)") + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
The dashed line is the share a random fifth of districts would capture. The margin over the survey's own regional averages is small per cell and concentrates where regions hold three to five districts. Under transport, burden captured is at chance: the transported product is an ordering and brings no targeting gain. Likely question: why the ceiling is only `r pc(Q$cap_oracle)`. Burden is spread across districts; even the true worst fifth holds under half of it.
:::

## What a correlation of `r f2(Q$infill_index)` means on the ground

::: {.notes}
DRAFT A of four candidate translations for a policy audience; keep one or two. The three readings are all computed from the same held-out predictions (in-fill, 5-fold by district, ten draws). Pairs: counted exactly from the held-out predictions (12_nce_targeting_metrics.R, PC-01: every pair of districts, ties excluded, mean over the 24 cells): the model orders `r pc(Q$pairs_pct)` of district pairs the way the survey does, the survey's own regional averages `r pc(Q$pairs_jk)`, a coin toss 50%; across borders (leave-one-country-out, `r Q$pairs_tr_cells` cells) it is `r pc(Q$pairs_pct_tr)`. A Spearman of `r f2(Q$infill_index)` sounds like more than it is: at district level it is six pairs in ten. The flagged fifth: deficiency prevalence in the fifth of districts the model ranks worst averages `r f2(Q$top20_prev_index, 1)`% against `r f2(Q$top20_prev_nat, 1)`% nationally (nce_targeting_summary.csv, mean over the 24 cells); a map that knew the truth would find `r f2(Q$top20_prev_oracle, 1)`%. Burden: the model's worst fifth holds `r pc(Q$cap_index)` of the deficient people, the survey's own regional averages `r pc(Q$cap_jk)`, a perfect map `r pc(Q$cap_oracle)`. The honest message is that the ranking is real but modest: it is better than the regional average a ministry would use today, and a long way from a map that knows every district, which is what the reliability ceiling explains.
:::

## How much of what a survey can see does the model recover?

::: {.notes}
DRAFT B. The question a decision-maker actually asks is not "is 0.40 high" but "compared with what". Two comparisons. Against the ceiling: a district estimate from the survey itself is noisy (one to three clusters per district), so even a perfect predictor of the true prevalence would correlate only `r f2(Q$vc_honest)` with what the survey reports; on that scale the model's `r f2(Q$infill_index_p)` (prevalence target) is `r pc(Q$ceiling_share)` of the attainable. Against current practice: the number a ministry would use for an unsurveyed district today is its region's average; the model beats it (`r f2(Q$infill_index)` against `r f2(Q$infill_jk)`, better in `r Q$infill_beats_jk` of `r Q$infill_paired` cells). Say plainly that the remaining gap is mostly the survey's noise, not the model's ignorance, and that the way to raise the ceiling is more clusters per district, which is the survey-design slide.
:::

## Right band, wrong band

::: {.notes}
DRAFT C. Policy runs on severity bands, not correlations: WHO's vitamin A bands are under 2%, 2 to 10, 10 to 20, 20% or more. With each district held out, the model puts `r pc(Q$rc_ex)` of districts in the band the survey puts them in and `r pc(Q$rc_w1)` within one band (risk_category_accuracy.csv, mean over the vitamin A cells); the survey's own regional averages give `r pc(Q$rc_jk_ex)` exact and `r pc(Q$rc_jk_w1)` within one band. Read the comparison honestly: on severity bands the survey's own regional averages do as well as the model or slightly better, because a band is mostly a level and the regional average carries the country's own level. The model is almost never two bands wrong (a district the survey calls severe is not called mild), and its case is not that it beats the regional average on bands but that it gives a band where there is no survey at all; in a new country the level comes from the national anchor (risk-class slide in the appendix has the transport rows). Use this slide only if the audience reads vitamin A or anaemia severity maps, and say the regional-average comparison aloud rather than letting the numbers sit.
:::

## Which decisions can the ranking carry?

::: {.notes}
DRAFT D. The correlation does not tell a programme whether the model is fit for a decision; this slide says which decisions, and which not. Yes: choosing which districts to visit, assess or enrol first, and where the next survey should put its clusters, because those need an order and the order is `r pc(Q$pairs_pct)` right at the pair level and better than the regional average. Yes: sequencing a roll-out across districts, for the same reason. With a national anchor only: a planning prevalence per district (`r f2(Q$ar_a1, 1)` points median error at a 5% national sample), because the ranking has no level of its own. No: reporting a district prevalence with no survey at all, or judging whether a programme worked, because the model is cross-sectional and validated on levels at one point in time, not on change. The decision rule to offer: use it where being roughly right about the order is enough, and pair it with a survey wherever a number has to be defended.
:::

```{r malawi-maps, fig.width=11, fig.height=5.6, dpi=130}
        pred[te, r] <- ARMS_V2[["domain_index"]](tr, te, Y, NULL, D, aux) } }
```

::: {.notes}
Malawi's 87 surveyed Traditional Authorities (grey: no survey clusters), the survey estimate beside the prediction made with each district held out (5-fold, ten draws). This is the protocol-v2 version of the January "what about subnational prevalence" maps: the same question, now scored under honest folds and with the index rather than the person-level ensemble. Women's B12 is the best in-fill cell of the `r Q$n_cells`; child iron is the outcome the Ghana map shows. The model orders districts; the survey's own estimate at a single-cluster district is itself noisy (reliability ceiling slide).
